chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: Sousa played straight; Army shaped character not music
summary: The band played Sousa straight, and the Army taught him discipline and appreciation of home.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, let me ask you this. The Sousa marches you played.
You played them straight like the white bands. There was no difference?
Oh yeah, because it was necessary. It would have been a crime to take a Sousa march, like "Stars and Stripes", or one of those other marches and mess with it.
Right. So in other words, your Army experience was more influential on you and your personality than it was -- it had no influence on your music.

Oh, absolutely, absolutely. It taught us that system was comfort. And how to obey, as well as be obeyed. You see. And it also taught us the value of things. Of leaving home. When you was over there and you couldn't get home, it taught you how to appreciate home.
